div.div: 2. CONSUMER TOPOLOGIES: POLLING, EVENT-DRIVEN & COMPETING CONSUMERS

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 246px; margin-left: 44px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #0F172A;

div.div:
Polling Consumer: Worker calls poll(timeout) on its own schedule.
Backpressure Control: Consumer never gets overwhelmed by burst traffic.
Event-Driven Push: Broker invokes callback immediately on arrival.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 389px; margin-left: 44px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #334155;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#334155, #acb8c9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
• Polling Overhead: Empty queue polling burns CPU without long-polling.
• Push Overflow: Fast publisher overwhelms slow receiver memory.
• Realization (Poll): Kafka Consumer poll loop, SQS ReceiveMessage.
• Realization (Push): Webhooks, RabbitMQ basic.consume, GCP Pub/Sub push.

box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #0F172A;

div.div:
Mechanic: Multiple worker instances read from a single shared queue.
Single Receiver: Each message delivered to exactly one active worker.
Elasticity: Scale workers up/down dynamically based on queue lag.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 389px; margin-left: 514px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #334155;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#334155, #acb8c9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
• Ordering Loss: Out-of-order execution inevitable under variable worker latency.
• Partition Assignment: In Kafka, concurrency is capped by partition count.
• Rebalance Storms: Worker heartbeats fail, triggering cluster-wide pauses.
• Realization: Kafka Consumer Groups, SQS competing worker pools.

div.div:
Selective Consumer: Filters messages using selector headers before delivery.
Message Dispatcher: Demuxes incoming channel across internal thread pool.
Service Activator: Invokes business method without messaging imports.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 389px; margin-left: 984px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #334155;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#334155, #acb8c9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
• Broker Performance: Complex JMS SQL-92 selectors degrade broker throughput.
• Thread Pool Saturation: Internal dispatcher queues can cause silent OOM.
• Virtual Threads: Java 21 eliminates OS thread exhaustion in dispatchers.
• Realization: Spring @JmsListener, JMS MessageSelectors, Camel Activator.

div.div: Protected by Deduplication Fences & Idempotent Processing ➔

div.div: 3. RELIABLE RECEIVERS: AT-LEAST-ONCE REALITY & DEDUPLICATION FENCES

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 448px; height: 1px; padding-top: 608px; margin-left: 29px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #0F172A;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#0F172A, #d3daea); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Idempotent Receiver (Atomic Token Lock)
• The Reality: Exactly-once delivery is physically impossible across open networks.
• Deduplication Table: Atomic INSERT of message_id in the same DB transaction.
• Duplicate Action: Primary key collision triggers immediate ACK and discard.
• Result: Effectively-once side-effect execution with zero duplicate state mutations.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 448px; height: 1px; padding-top: 608px; margin-left: 499px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #0F172A;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#0F172A, #d3daea); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Poison Pill Quarantine & Dead Letter Handling
• Poison Pill: A malformed message that crashes the consumer deserializer every time.
• Infinite Loop: Worker crashes ➔ message returns to queue ➔ worker crashes again.
• Circuit Breaker: Max delivery count exceeded ➔ divert to Dead Letter Channel.
• Operator Redrive: Quarantine preserves payload for schema patch & manual re-injection.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 448px; height: 1px; padding-top: 608px; margin-left: 969px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000; background-color: #FFFFFF;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#000000, #ededed); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; background-color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Enterprise Architectural Invariants
• Never Dual-Write: Never update a local DB and emit a message in separate uncoordinated calls.
• Deduplication TTL: Dedup tables must define sliding retention windows to prevent disk exhaustion.
• Fencing Tokens: State mutations must assert monotonic version increments (v_fence > v_current).
